# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_config_reference.py from trader.ops.config.Settings. -->
<!-- Do not edit by hand: describe the field in config.py and regenerate. -->

Every setting is an environment variable read by `trader.ops.config.Settings` (pydantic-settings, prefix `TRADER_`, names case-insensitive). Values also load from a `.env` file in the working directory; real environment variables outrank it. Copy [`.env.example`](../.env.example) to `.env` to start. Regenerate this page and the example with `uv run python scripts/gen_config_reference.py`; CI runs it with `--check`.

## Categories

- **gate** — fail-closed safety switch. The default is the closed position; flipping it changes what can reach the venue or the decide prompt. Flip through the runbook, one at a time.
- **tuning** — numeric or behavioral parameter; changing it never opens a door by itself.
- **endpoint** — where a dependency lives: a URL, a served model id, or a path.
- **credential** — a secret. Blank means that integration stays off; never commit a value.

Gates at a glance (all default closed):

- `TRADER_AUTH_DISABLED` = `false`
- `TRADER_ALPACA_LIVE_ENABLED` = `false`
- `TRADER_SHADOW_MODE` = `true`
- `TRADER_LOOP_ENABLED` = `false`
- `TRADER_SHADOW_SYMBOLS` = *(empty)*
- `TRADER_EXIT_REVIEW_ENABLED` = `false`
- `TRADER_BRIEFS_ENABLED` = `false`
- `TRADER_DESK_ENABLED` = `false`
- `TRADER_SETTLEMENT_ENABLED` = `false`
- `TRADER_LESSONS_ENABLED` = `false`
- `TRADER_SENTIMENT_TRIGGER_ENABLED` = `false`
- `TRADER_POLYMARKET_IN_MACRO_VIEW` = `false`
- `TRADER_CALLS_ENABLED` = `false`
- `TRADER_CONFIRM_VETO_ENABLED` = `true`

## Surfaces / auth

The API, MCP server and CLI share one service registry; auth guards the first two.

| Variable | Type | Default | Category | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TRADER_API_KEY` | `str` | *(empty)* | credential | Bearer key the API and MCP surfaces require. Mandatory outside dev: an unset key with `TRADER_AUTH_DISABLED` unset refuses to boot. |
| `TRADER_CAPTURE_API_KEY` | `str` | *(empty)* | credential | Capture-scoped second key for external research agents (Hermes). It may only submit, list and retire research notes and read the Macro View: on REST those four routes (plus `/health`), on MCP the `/mcp-capture/` mount alone. Every other route and `/mcp/` answer 403. Blank means no capture key exists; it never substitutes for `TRADER_API_KEY`. |
| `TRADER_AUTH_DISABLED` | `bool` | `false` | gate | Explicit dev opt-out from API auth. Without it, an unset `TRADER_API_KEY` fails boot (fail closed). Never set on a reachable box. |
| `TRADER_API_BASE_URL` | `str` | `http://localhost:8080` | endpoint | Where the CLI finds the running API. |

## Store

One Postgres holds everything durable. Market data is never stored (fetch-on-tick).

| Variable | Type | Default | Category | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TRADER_DATABASE_URL` | `str` | `postgresql://trader:trader@localhost:5544/trader` | endpoint | Postgres DSN for the journal, ledger, research store and audit log. The test suite appends `_test` to it and truncates that sibling database. |

## Safety gates

Paper only. The LLM proposes, RiskGuard disposes, the broker executes; no setting bypasses that chain.

| Variable | Type | Default | Category | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TRADER_ALPACA_LIVE_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | gate | Live Alpaca client construction refuses unless this is `true`. Paper only by default; there is no other path to a live venue. |

## Decide loop

The background scheduler: what it watches, how often, and whether it submits.

| Variable | Type | Default | Category | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TRADER_SHADOW_MODE` | `bool` | `true` | gate | Shadow mode defaults ON: the pipeline runs and journals every decision, and submits nothing. Set `false` to let RiskGuard-approved intents reach the paper broker. |
| `TRADER_LOOP_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | gate | Runs the background decide loop inside the API process. An explicit operator opt-in; off, the surfaces still serve but nothing ticks. |
| `TRADER_LOOP_TICK_SECONDS` | `float` | `60.0` | tuning | Seconds between scheduler ticks (quote fetch, mark, trigger evaluation). |
| `TRADER_LOOP_MAX_HEARTBEATS_PER_TICK` | `int` | `0` | tuning | Cap on heartbeat wakeups per tick (0 = no cap). Set it when the watchlist is large: heartbeats beyond the cap wait for the next tick, most overdue first, so startup, each cadence and each market open do not burst the data API's rate limit. Price-move, vol-spike and sentiment triggers are never capped. |
| `TRADER_LOOP_MAX_CONCURRENT_DECIDES` | `int` | `2` | tuning | How many Bots may call the decide model at once (at least 1). The Supervisor runs every Bot each tick; the rest wait for a free slot, so adding a Bot does not multiply the load on a self-hosted model. |
| `TRADER_LOOP_SYMBOLS` | `str` | `BTC/USD,ETH/USD` | tuning | Comma-separated symbols the loop watches and may trade. |
| `TRADER_EXTRA_SYMBOLS` | `str` | *(empty)* | tuning | Comma-separated US-listed stocks or ETFs added to the symbol universe, minted long-only on the NYSE calendar. Adding a name here makes it known; it is watched only when also listed in `TRADER_LOOP_SYMBOLS`, and a new name should shadow via `TRADER_SHADOW_SYMBOLS` before it may submit. |
| `TRADER_SHADOW_SYMBOLS` | `str` | *(empty)* | gate | Per-symbol shadow: comma-separated tickers that decide and risk-check but never submit, while the rest of the build trades live-paper. A new symbol earns its flip here first. |
| `TRADER_EXIT_REVIEW_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | gate | Exit-review lane: with a position held, the decide prompt gains a held-position block (entry, age, unrealized P&L, latest sentiment) and an explicit ask whether the thesis still holds: `close`/reduce if not, `hold` if so. Advisory only, RiskGuard never sees it. A decide-behavior change: flip only through `docs/runbooks/decide-change-gate.md` (replay it with `trader eval run --exit-review --seed-qty --seed-entry`). |
| `TRADER_SHADOW_SIGNALS_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | tuning | Bot #1 subscribes to the shadow signals (#144), the Kronos forecast and the crypto derivatives reading: each is read on every decide and journaled in `decisions.signals` for scoring, never shown to the decide (a Bot defined in the store subscribes in its spec instead). Changes no decision. See `docs/runbooks/shadow-signals.md`. |
| `TRADER_KRONOS_URL` | `str` | *(empty)* | endpoint | Base URL of the Kronos forecast sidecar (`infra/kronos/`), e.g. `http://localhost:8095`. Blank = no Kronos reading. The trader decides as usual when the sidecar is down; that decide journals no forecast. |
| `TRADER_KRONOS_PATHS` | `int` | `32` | tuning | Independent sampled paths per Kronos forecast; the band (p10/p90) and the share of paths up are taken across them. |
| `TRADER_SIGNAL_HORIZON_BARS` | `int` | `24` | tuning | Horizon the shadow signals are forecast and scored at, in 1h bars: Kronos samples this many bars ahead, and every signal is scored against the return this many bars after it was read. |
| `TRADER_DERIVATIVES_VENUES` | `str` | `binance,bybit,okx` | endpoint | Comma-separated ccxt venues the crypto derivatives Source reads BTC and ETH USDT perpetuals from (public endpoints, no keys). Empty = no reading. |
| `TRADER_SHADOW_EQUITY` | `float` | `100000.0` | tuning | Equity the risk chain assumes in shadow builds (no broker). Live-paper builds read equity from the broker and keep the last good value when it is down. |

## Risk limits (RiskGuard)

Deterministic limits applied to every intent. Code and config only, never prompt-driven; a change here is a risk-chain behavior change and goes through the decide-change gate.

| Variable | Type | Default | Category | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TRADER_RISK_MAX_POSITION_FRAC` | `float` | `0.1` | tuning | Max notional of one position as a fraction of equity. |
| `TRADER_RISK_MIN_NOTIONAL_USD` | `float` | `5.0` | tuning | Opens below this notional are denied (no dust orders), clamps included. |
| `TRADER_RISK_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS` | `int` | `5` | tuning | Max open positions; a new open beyond it is denied, adds and exits pass. |
| `TRADER_RISK_MAX_TRADES_PER_DAY` | `int` | `20` | tuning | Max submitted trades per UTC day, counted across symbols. |
| `TRADER_RISK_DAILY_LOSS_LIMIT_FRAC` | `float` | `0.03` | tuning | Daily loss breaker: equity down this fraction from the session start halts opens until an operator resumes it. |
| `TRADER_RISK_WEEKLY_DRAWDOWN_LIMIT_FRAC` | `float` | `0.1` | tuning | Weekly drawdown breaker, same mechanics as the daily limit. |
| `TRADER_RISK_APPROVAL_NOTIONAL_USD` | `float` | `1000.0` | tuning | Unattended opens above this notional clamp down to it and execute; the clamp is journaled. Exits are never clamped. |
| `TRADER_RISK_PARK_ABOVE_USD` | `float` | `0.0` | tuning | `0` disables parking. A value above the approval cap parks larger opens for a human (`trader risk approve`); everything between the cap and this band clamps to the cap and executes unattended. |
| `TRADER_RISK_STOP_LOSS_FRAC` | `float` | `0.08` | tuning | Deterministic stop, and its ceiling: when a held position's loss against its entry reaches its stop (this fraction, or tighter under `TRADER_RISK_STOP_VOL_MULT`) on two ticks in a row, the loop closes the whole position without asking the model. `0` turns it off. Pause and drift still block it. |
| `TRADER_RISK_STOP_VOL_MULT` | `float` | `2.0` | tuning | Volatility-scaled stop: the stop sits this many of the symbol's typical daily moves (its 1h realized volatility scaled to a day) below the entry, never wider than `TRADER_RISK_STOP_LOSS_FRAC`. With no volatility reading the fixed stop applies. `0` keeps the fixed stop alone. Chosen in `docs/reports/2026-10-22-bot-1-exits.md`. |
| `TRADER_RISK_STOP_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` | `int` | `86400` | tuning | After a stop closes a symbol, RiskGuard refuses opens on it for this long. |
| `TRADER_RISK_MIN_HOLD_SECONDS` | `int` | `14400` | tuning | Minimum hold: RiskGuard denies the model's close of a position its Bot opened less than this long ago. The deterministic stop is never held, so it is what protects a fresh position. `0` turns the hold off. Chosen in `docs/reports/2026-10-30-sentiment-churn.md`. |
| `TRADER_RISK_NO_TRADE_BAND_FRAC` | `float` | `0.01` | tuning | No-trade band: RiskGuard denies an open or add whose notional, after the sizing clamps, is below this fraction of the Bot's Sleeve (the account for a whole-account Bot); a smaller order pays spread and fees for a move it barely changes. Trims, closes and the stop always pass. `0` turns the band off. |
| `TRADER_RISK_EARNINGS_BLACKOUT_DAYS` | `int` | `1` | tuning | Earnings blackout: RiskGuard denies an open or add on a US stock from this many sessions before its earnings report through the report session (verdict `earnings_blackout`). Closes, trims and the stop always pass. The report date comes from the OpenBB producer's earnings rows (`TRADER_OPENBB_BASE_URL`); with no row for the symbol, or one older than 3 days, the check fails open with a logged warning and its verdict says so. `0` turns the blackout off. |

## Replay costs

What a replayed fill pays (`trader eval run`), so a replay reports net P&L beside gross. Replay only: the live loop's fills are the venue's. Every knob at `0` is free.

| Variable | Type | Default | Category | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TRADER_REPLAY_HALF_SPREAD_BPS_EQUITY` | `float` | `5.0` | tuning | Half the bid-ask spread, in basis points, a replayed equity or ETF fill pays when replay has no real quote (it has none today: its quote is the last close on both sides). A real quote's own half-spread is used when there is one. `0` turns the spread off for equities and ETFs. |
| `TRADER_REPLAY_HALF_SPREAD_BPS_CRYPTO` | `float` | `10.0` | tuning | The same fallback half-spread for a replayed crypto fill. `0` turns the spread off for crypto. |
| `TRADER_REPLAY_FEE_BPS` | `float` | `2.0` | tuning | A fee every replayed fill pays, in basis points of its notional (regulatory and clearing fees, rounded up). `0` turns it off. |
| `TRADER_REPLAY_CRYPTO_TAKER_FEE_BPS` | `float` | `25.0` | tuning | Alpaca's crypto taker fee, in basis points, paid by a replayed crypto fill on top of `TRADER_REPLAY_FEE_BPS`. 25 is the taker rate of Alpaca's lowest-volume tier (its maker rate there is 15); a higher tier pays less. `0` turns it off. |
| `TRADER_REPLAY_IMPACT_COEF` | `float` | `1.0` | tuning | Square-root market impact: a replayed fill moves its price by this coefficient times the symbol's daily volatility times the square root of the order's share of average daily dollar volume (Almgren et al. 2005; fits put it between 0.5 and 1.0, so 1.0 is the conservative end). Volume and volatility come from the step's own 1h bars. `0` turns it off. |

## Research Desk

Notes, Macro View compilation, briefs, the decision desk and X sentiment. Every flag here is dark by default and earns its flip through replay, then a shadow window.

| Variable | Type | Default | Category | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TRADER_RESEARCH_STALE_DAYS` | `int` | `30` | tuning | Days before an unpinned note auto-stales out of compilation (retire stays explicit). |
| `TRADER_RESEARCH_COMPILE_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS` | `float` | `30.0` | tuning | Quiet window after the last note change before the Macro View recompiles. |
| `TRADER_RESEARCH_MIRROR_DIR` | `str` | `research` | tuning | One-way markdown mirror folder (gitignored, regenerable). Empty disables. |
| `TRADER_BRIEFS_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | gate | Per-candidate briefs: briefs compile and store on note changes regardless; this flag alone lets them into the decide prompt. A decide-behavior change: flip only through `docs/runbooks/decide-change-gate.md`. |
| `TRADER_DESK_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | gate | Decision desk: analyst fan-out + cross-model critic around the decide. Dark by default; earns its flip via replay desk-on vs desk-off, then a shadow window. |
| `TRADER_DESK_CRITIC_DAILY_USD` | `float` | `1.0` | tuning | Default Spend cap for the critic Role, USD per UTC day (#108; a cap set on any surface replaces it). At the cap the critic's paid models sit out the day and a free one in its Chain reviews; with none, reviews are journaled pass-throughs. |
| `TRADER_SETTLEMENT_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | gate | Learning loop (#143): a background pass settles every journaled decision 5 trading days on (forward and excess return from daily bars, fetched on use) and lets the `reflect` Role write a Lesson for the newest settled ones. Off, nothing settles on its own; the `settle_decisions` command still runs one pass. Lessons reach a decide prompt only through a Bot's `lessons` Source. |
| `TRADER_SETTLEMENT_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | `float` | `3600.0` | tuning | Seconds between settlement passes when `TRADER_SETTLEMENT_ENABLED`. |
| `TRADER_REFLECT_MAX_PER_PASS` | `int` | `10` | tuning | Most Lessons the `reflect` Role writes per settlement pass, newest settled decisions first; the rest wait for the next pass. `0` settles without Lessons. The Role's Spend cap still bounds the day. |
| `TRADER_LESSONS_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | gate | Bot #1 reads its `lessons` Source: its latest settled Lessons on the symbol go into the decide prompt. Other Bots subscribe in their spec. A decide-behavior change: flip only through `docs/runbooks/decide-change-gate.md`. |
| `TRADER_SENTIMENT_POLL_SECONDS` | `float` | `10800.0` | tuning | X sentiment poll interval for held symbols; needs an xAI credential (x_search runs server-side on xAI). The daily call cap still bounds a shorter interval. |
| `TRADER_SENTIMENT_DAILY_CALL_CAP` | `int` | `24` | tuning | Max sentiment polls per UTC day across symbols. |
| `TRADER_SENTIMENT_TRIGGER_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | gate | Lets a sentiment swing wake the decide loop. Shadow-first: leave OFF until at least a week of journaled scores looks sane. Code default off; a live book arms it in `.env`, never here. |
| `TRADER_SENTIMENT_SWING_THRESHOLD` | `float` | `0.5` | tuning | Score move between polls that wakes the trader; scores are on [-1, 1]. |
| `TRADER_SENTIMENT_X_HANDLES` | `str` | *(empty)* | tuning | Comma-separated allowlist of X handles for x_search; empty = open search. |
| `TRADER_OPENBB_BASE_URL` | `str` | *(empty)* | endpoint | The OpenBB sidecar (`openbb-api`, its own venv or container; `docs/runbooks/deploy.md`), e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:6900` (`http://openbb:6900` inside compose). The OpenBB producer (`trader openbb refresh`, on a timer) reads keyless providers through it and writes the `earnings`, `options` and `fundamentals` Sources a Bot may subscribe to, plus the earnings blackout's report dates. Empty: no producer; those Sources are absent and the blackout fails open. The trader never imports OpenBB and never waits on it to decide. |
| `TRADER_POLYMARKET_TOPICS` | `str` | `Fed decision,CPI,recession` | tuning | Comma-separated Polymarket search topics for the `polymarket` Source (#142); each keeps its most-traded open markets. Polymarket is keyless and fetched only while some Bot subscribes to the Source. |
| `TRADER_POLYMARKET_IN_MACRO_VIEW` | `bool` | `false` | gate | Lets the latest Polymarket odds into the Macro View compiler's inputs, citable as `[poly:<id>]`. The Macro View feeds every Bot, so this is a decide-behavior change for all of them: flip only through `docs/runbooks/decide-change-gate.md`. |
| `TRADER_SCREENER_MIN_DOLLAR_VOLUME_USD` | `float` | `50000000.0` | tuning | Screener liquidity floor: symbols whose 20-day average dollar volume (close x volume) is below this are skipped before ranking. The screener is a query (`GET /screener`, `get_screener`, `trader screener run`); it is not wired into the decide loop. |
| `TRADER_SCREENER_LOOKBACK_DAYS` | `int` | `90` | tuning | Daily bars the screener fetches per symbol (one or two multi-symbol Alpaca requests per query, nothing stored). Must cover the 60-day momentum window: at least 61 trading days; 90 leaves slack for holidays. |
| `TRADER_SEAT_MODEL` | `str` | `grok-4.3` | endpoint | Grok model for the desk seats (`trader seat run <seat>`, a standalone process outside `trader-api`). Must be entitled on `/v1/responses` with `x_search` and `web_search` (probe matrix: docs/research/xai-api.md). The seat authenticates with the shared SuperGrok OAuth login by default (cross-process refresh lock, #68); `--credential api_key` pins `XAI_API_KEY` instead. |
| `TRADER_SEAT_MAX_NOTES` | `int` | `3` | tuning | Hard cap on notes one seat sweep may submit after the grounding and dedupe gates; the rest are dropped and logged. |
| `TRADER_SEAT_NOTE_MAX_CHARS` | `int` | `1400` | tuning | Seat note body cap. A longer body is sent back to the model to distill once; still over → dropped. Keeps notes inside the decide prompt's research lane. |
| `TRADER_SEAT_STATE_PATH` | `str` | `~/.local/state/trader/seat-runs.jsonl` | tuning | Append-only JSONL of seat runs (submitted note ids, usage, estimated cost). The seat runs outside the service meter, so this is its spend record; `trader seat report` reads it back for the citation loop. |

## Telegram calls

The Telegram channel-calls scorecard (Phase 1): read one signals channel read-only, parse each call once and score it against bars. It places no orders; the poller is dark until `TRADER_CALLS_ENABLED` is flipped.

| Variable | Type | Default | Category | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TRADER_CALLS_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | gate | Runs the Telegram channel-calls poller: reads the configured channel (read-only, never sends or marks read), parses each post's call once and scores it against bars. Phase 1 places no orders. Needs a stored Telegram session. |
| `TRADER_CALLS_CHANNEL_ID` | `int` | `-1003097376178` | tuning | Telegram channel the calls poller reads. Only this channel is read. |
| `TRADER_CALLS_POLL_SECONDS` | `float` | `300.0` | tuning | Seconds between polls of the calls channel. |
| `TRADER_CALLS_RECHECK_POSTS` | `int` | `50` | tuning | How many of the newest posts each poll re-reads for edits; an edit is stored as a new version and never re-parses a live call's levels. |
| `TRADER_CALLS_SESSION_NAME` | `str` | `spark` | tuning | Name of the stored Telegram session (`channel_sessions`, Fernet-encrypted with `TRADER_SECRETS_KEY`) the poller logs in with. |
| `TRADER_CALLS_SLEEVE_USD` | `float` | `10000.0` | tuning | Notional sleeve the scorecard sizes calls against: size per call = sleeve x allocation x leverage (1% and 1x when the call omits them). Reported only. |

## LLM endpoints

Two roles, each any OpenAI-compatible `/v1`: **decide** (also the desk analysts) and **research** (briefs, compiler, critic, registry sentiment). With `TRADER_DECIDE_BASE_URL` empty, decide uses the **Nemotron preset** (`TRADER_NEMOTRON_*`), whose client forces `chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: false}` on every request; the Spark endpoint collapses to ~0.35 tok/s without it. A generic URL that equals the Nemotron base URL gets the same flag; any other URL never receives `chat_template_kwargs`, because vendor APIs such as OpenAI reject it. Research falls back to xAI when configured, else to the decide client; `x_search` sentiment is xAI-only.

| Variable | Type | Default | Category | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TRADER_NEMOTRON_BASE_URL` | `str` | `http://localhost:8009/v1` | endpoint | Nemotron preset: a self-hosted vLLM `/v1` (default :8009, no auth). Used for decide and analysts when `TRADER_DECIDE_BASE_URL` is empty; the preset client sends `chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: false}` on every request (without it the endpoint collapses to ~0.35 tok/s). A generic URL equal to this one gets the same flag forced on. Inside compose, point it at `http://host.docker.internal:8009/v1`. |
| `TRADER_NEMOTRON_MODEL` | `str` | `nemotron-3-super` | endpoint | Served model id on the Nemotron vLLM. Swapping the decide model on an existing box is a decide-behavior change (`docs/runbooks/decide-change-gate.md`); for a new user it is simply the first run. |
| `TRADER_DECIDE_BASE_URL` | `str` | *(empty)* | endpoint | Any OpenAI-compatible `/v1` for the decide (and analyst) role: OpenAI, Groq, Together, Ollama, vLLM, xAI. Empty selects the Nemotron preset above, which is the only client that sends `chat_template_kwargs`; a vendor API such as OpenAI rejects that argument, so it is never sent to a generic URL. |
| `TRADER_DECIDE_MODEL` | `str` | *(empty)* | endpoint | Model id at `TRADER_DECIDE_BASE_URL` (ignored under the Nemotron preset). |
| `TRADER_DECIDE_API_KEY` | `str` | *(empty)* | credential | Bearer key for `TRADER_DECIDE_BASE_URL`; blank for unauthenticated hosts. |
| `TRADER_DECIDE_EXTRA_BODY` | `str` | *(empty)* | tuning | JSON object merged into every chat-completions body for the decide client (e.g. `{"reasoning_effort": "low"}`). Must parse as an object. Ollama / llama.cpp ignore `chat_template_kwargs`; their no-thinking switch is `{"reasoning_effort": "none"}`. Without it a reasoning model burns the decide token budget thinking and returns empty content. |
| `TRADER_DECIDE_PRICE_IN` | `float` | `0.0` | tuning | USD per 1M input tokens for the decide model. `0` reads the built-in PRICES table, else $0 (logged once); non-zero overrides the table. |
| `TRADER_DECIDE_PRICE_OUT` | `float` | `0.0` | tuning | USD per 1M output tokens for the decide model; same rules as the input price. |
| `TRADER_CONFIRM_PROVIDER` | `str` | *(empty)* | endpoint | Empty: no Confirm. `jev`: TypeSafe's Jev judgment model is asked about every open or close Draft (`TRADER_CONFIRM_*`) and its judgments are journaled in the decision's `confirm` column. It can only veto an open (a hold instead, behind `TRADER_CONFIRM_VETO_ENABLED`); a close is recorded, never vetoed. |
| `TRADER_CONFIRM_BASE_URL` | `str` | `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` | endpoint | Jev's judgment endpoint for the confirm role. |
| `TRADER_CONFIRM_MODEL` | `str` | `jev-latest` | endpoint | Jev model id for the confirm role. |
| `TRADER_CONFIRM_API_KEY` | `str` | *(empty)* | credential | TypeSafe API key for the confirm role; required when `TRADER_CONFIRM_PROVIDER=jev`. Errors report the HTTP status only. |
| `TRADER_CONFIRM_VETO_ENABLED` | `bool` | `true` | gate | Veto a proposed open when the confirm role's judgments fail the rule in loop/confirm_questions.py. Off: still asked and recorded as would_veto. |
| `TRADER_RESEARCH_BASE_URL` | `str` | *(empty)* | endpoint | Same shape as the decide endpoint, for the brief, compiler, critic and registry sentiment roles. Empty keeps xAI if configured, else the decide client. x_search stays xAI-only. |
| `TRADER_RESEARCH_MODEL` | `str` | *(empty)* | endpoint | Model id at `TRADER_RESEARCH_BASE_URL`. |
| `TRADER_RESEARCH_API_KEY` | `str` | *(empty)* | credential | Bearer key for `TRADER_RESEARCH_BASE_URL`. |
| `TRADER_RESEARCH_EXTRA_BODY` | `str` | *(empty)* | tuning | JSON object merged into the research roles' chat-completions bodies. On Ollama / llama.cpp use `{"reasoning_effort": "none"}` to turn thinking off (`chat_template_kwargs` is ignored there); otherwise a reasoning model spends the token budget thinking and returns empty content. |
| `TRADER_RESEARCH_PRICE_IN` | `float` | `0.0` | tuning | USD per 1M input tokens for the research model (`0` = PRICES table, else $0). |
| `TRADER_RESEARCH_PRICE_OUT` | `float` | `0.0` | tuning | USD per 1M output tokens for the research model. |
| `TRADER_XAI_BASE_URL` | `str` | `https://api.x.ai/v1` | endpoint | xAI API base for Grok research roles and x_search sentiment. |
| `TRADER_XAI_MODEL` | `str` | `grok-4` | endpoint | Grok model id for the xAI research roles. |
| `TRADER_REFLECT_XAI_MODEL` | `str` | `grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning` | endpoint | Grok model id for the `reflect` Role on the xAI chain (a non-reasoning model: a Lesson is a short summary). An explicit research endpoint or a Profile replaces it. |
| `XAI_API_KEY` (alias `TRADER_XAI_API_KEY`) | `str` | *(empty)* | credential | xAI API key: first-class fallback when SuperGrok OAuth is absent or quarantined. Provider-conventional name; the `TRADER_` form is accepted too. |
| `TRADER_XAI_TOKEN_KEY` | `str` | *(empty)* | credential | SuperGrok device-code OAuth: Fernet key that encrypts the token store. Set it, then run `trader xai login`. Generate with `python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"`. Unset, OAuth is disabled and the provider resolves to `XAI_API_KEY` alone. |
| `TRADER_SECRETS_KEY` | `str` | *(empty)* | credential | Fernet key that encrypts Provider API keys stored in Postgres by the model picker. Generate with `python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"`. Unset, Providers that need a key cannot be added; keyless local Providers still work. Losing it loses the stored keys. |
| `TRADER_XAI_TOKEN_PATH` | `str` | `~/.config/trader/xai_token.enc` | tuning | Encrypted SuperGrok OAuth token store path. |

## Broker / market data credentials

Provider-conventional names without the prefix are the primary spelling; the `TRADER_`-prefixed alias is accepted too.

| Variable | Type | Default | Category | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ALPACA_API_KEY_ID` (alias `TRADER_ALPACA_API_KEY_ID`) | `str` | *(empty)* | credential | Alpaca paper key id. The same keys serve broker and market data. Rate-limit budget (Basic/free tier): ~200 req/min across data endpoints; crypto data free; equities = IEX feed only. Fetch-on-tick load is ~2 req/wakeup/symbol, far below budget. |
| `ALPACA_API_SECRET` (alias `TRADER_ALPACA_API_SECRET`) | `str` | *(empty)* | credential | Alpaca paper secret, paired with `ALPACA_API_KEY_ID`. |
| `TWELVE_DATA_API_KEY` (alias `TRADER_TWELVE_DATA_API_KEY`) | `str` | *(empty)* | credential | Twelve Data key, equities-quote fallback only (untouched unless Alpaca equities data fails). Free tier: 8 credits/min, 800/day, 1 credit per quote or time_series call. |
| `FRED_API_KEY` (alias `TRADER_FRED_API_KEY`) | `str` | *(empty)* | credential | FRED key (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/api_key.html) for the macro context line; responses are TTL-cached 1h in-process, so live load is a few calls/day. Absent, the decide prompt carries no FRED line. |
| `TRADER_SEC_EDGAR_USER_AGENT` (alias `SEC_EDGAR_USER_AGENT`) | `str` | *(empty)* | credential | Who SEC EDGAR sees for the `sec_filings` Source (#142): a name and a contact address, e.g. `Salamander research ops@example.org`. EDGAR is free and keyless but refuses anonymous callers (https://www.sec.gov/os/accessing-edgar-data). Not a secret, but an identity: blank leaves the EDGAR producer out of the build. |
